title: Filling in "details unknown" sessions: "Voodoo," "Poinciana" and "Dolphin Street Boogie"
summary: He identifies sidemen on a label's dates and recalls fans asking him to sign an old 78 of "Voodoo" at a Sacramento festival.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well, do you know any of the ones that are listed as unknown?

Let's see. Including Maxwell Davis or Bumps Myers. Most of the time I had both of them on the date, on the same date. Their styles were very similar. But this was... I did some things for that company that I like very much. One was "Voodoo," which I know you never heard, but I happened to be up in Sacramento on one of those...what do you call them... They had these things up there every year...

They have a Dixieland Jubilee. So I went up there and played, and a lot of people were, "Hey, 'Voodoo'!" And I couldn't even remember what they were talking about. Then somebody came up with an old '78 record that they wanted me to autograph, in perfect shape. "Tonight Of All

Nights" was one of my tunes, "How Come Baby?" and... The best thing that I remember doing was "Poinciana". I love that tune anyhow -- "Song Of The Trees." And on the other side of that was "Dolphin Street Boogie," which was the theme of that station. So I've changed the name of that. Now we call it "I'll See You Later, So Long." Mary Lou, my wife, wrote a lyric to it. And that's one of the things we did...
At the concert at Santa Monica.
And then we did "Basin Street Blues," "Glow Worm"... That's the time when the Mills Brothers had a hit record on "Glow Worm", so I did "Glow Worm"... Oh, it was fun.
